CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Set the SHELL option -o pipefail before RUN with a pipe in it. If you are using /bin/sh in an alpine image or if your shell is symlinked to busybox then consider explicitly setting your SHELL to /bin/ash, or disable this check

When a pipe fails in bash/sh without pipefail, only the exit code of the last command is checked, potentially hiding errors in earlier commands. This is a best practice violation that can lead to silent failures during image builds. The default shell in SUSE Linux Enterprise (SLE) base images is typically /bin/sh, which may or may not support pipefail depending on whether it's linked to bash or another shell. To ensure robust error handling, the SHELL instruction should be added before any RUN command that uses pipes to explicitly set the shell to one that supports pipefail (like /bin/bash) and enable the pipefail option.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: [DL4006](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint/wiki/DL4006): Add a SHELL instruction immediately after the FROM statement to set the shell to /bin/bash with the -o pipefail option enabled. This ensures that any command failure in a pipeline will cause the entire RUN command to fail, preventing silent errors. Insert 'SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]' as line 2, right after the FROM instruction on line 1. This will apply to all subsequent RUN commands in the Dockerfile. The -o pipefail option makes the pipeline return the exit status of the last command to exit with a non-zero status, or zero if all commands exit successfully. This is a Docker best practice for production-grade images.

CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Use arguments JSON notation for CMD and ENTRYPOINT arguments
FAULT_DESCRIPTION: The HEALTHCHECK instruction on line 117-118 uses shell form with the CMD keyword followed by a shell command string. Hadolint flags this because shell form spawns a shell process (/bin/sh -c) to execute the command, which can cause problems with signal propagation (like SIGTERM during container shutdown) and makes the process tree more complex. The shell form also makes it harder to predict exact behavior across different base images. JSON array notation (exec form) is preferred because it executes the command directly without invoking a shell, providing more predictable behavior and better signal handling. This is especially important for health checks that run periodically throughout the container's lifetime.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: Convert the HEALTHCHECK CMD from shell form to JSON array notation (exec form). Replace the shell command with a JSON array where each argument is a separate string element. Since the current health check uses a Node.js one-liner with shell features, you need to invoke the shell explicitly in the JSON array format using ["/bin/sh", "-c", "command"]. This maintains the same functionality while using the recommended exec form. The fix changes line 118 from 'CMD node -e "require...' to 'CMD ["/bin/sh", "-c", "node -e \"require..."]'. Note that quotes inside the command string need to be escaped with backslashes in the JSON format.

CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
FAULT_DESCRIPTION: The method at line 517 uses Math.random() to generate passwords, which is a pseudorandom number generator not designed for cryptographic purposes. Math.random() is predictable and can be exploited by attackers who can observe or influence the seed state. For security-sensitive operations like password generation, cryptographically secure random number generators must be used. In Node.js, the crypto module provides crypto.randomInt() and crypto.randomBytes() which use the operating system's cryptographically secure random number generator. This is a real vulnerability because the generated passwords could be predicted or brute-forced more easily than passwords generated with proper cryptographic randomness.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomInt() from Node.js's built-in crypto module. First, add an import statement at the top of the file: import crypto from 'crypto'. Then modify the generatePassword method to use crypto.randomInt(charset.length) instead of Math.floor(Math.random() * charset.length). This ensures that password generation uses cryptographically secure random values that cannot be predicted by attackers. The crypto module is a standard Node.js module and requires no additional dependencies.

CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Prototype Pollution
FAULT_DESCRIPTION: The _filterTenantData method iterates over all properties of the tenant object using Object.entries() and assigns them directly to a new filtered object without validation (line 120: filtered[key] = value). If the tenant object contains properties like '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype', this assignment could pollute the Object prototype chain, affecting all objects in the application. The data flow shows that tenant data originates from line 89 (the data parameter) and flows to line 120 where the unsafe assignment occurs. This is particularly dangerous because tenant data comes from external sources (the tenantManager) and could potentially be manipulated by attackers if they can control tenant properties through the HANA Cloud API or database.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: Add property name validation to prevent prototype pollution by checking against dangerous property names before assignment. Use Object.hasOwnProperty.call() to ensure we're only copying own properties, and explicitly block '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' properties. Additionally, use Object.create(null) to create the filtered object without a prototype chain, providing defense in depth. This ensures that even if dangerous properties exist in the source object, they cannot pollute the prototype chain or be assigned to the filtered object.

(4) The Content-Type is set to 'application/json', which browsers will not execute as HTML/JavaScript. CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
FAULT_DESCRIPTION: At line 517, the code uses Math.random() to generate a password by selecting random characters from a charset. Math.random() is a pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) that is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted by attackers who observe its output patterns. For security-sensitive operations like password generation, cryptographically secure random number generators must be used. In Node.js, the crypto module provides crypto.randomInt() which uses a cryptographically secure random number generator suitable for security purposes. This vulnerability is real because the generated password could be used for authentication or access control, and a weak random source makes it vulnerable to prediction attacks.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: Replace Math.random() with Node.js's crypto.randomInt() function to generate cryptographically secure random numbers. First, import the crypto module at the top of the file. Then, modify the generatePassword method to use crypto.randomInt(charset.length) instead of Math.floor(Math.random() * charset.length). This ensures that the password generation uses a cryptographically secure random number generator that cannot be predicted by attackers. The crypto module is built into Node.js and provides FIPS-compliant random number generation suitable for security-critical operations.

Without setting the SHELL option with -o pipefail, if any command in the pipeline fails (except the last one), the failure may be silently ignored, and the Docker build will continue as if nothing went wrong. This is particularly dangerous in this case because the RUN command performs critical operations like downloading certificates, adding repositories, and installing packages. If any intermediate command fails (e.g., curl fails to download a certificate or zypper fails to add a repository), the build might succeed but produce a broken image. The -o pipefail option ensures that the entire pipeline fails if any command in it fails, making the build process more reliable and preventing silent failures.

Insert 'SHELL ["/bin/sh", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]' between line 1 (the FROM instruction) and line 2 (the first RUN command). This will ensure that any failure in the piped commands will cause the entire RUN command to fail, making the build process more robust and preventing silent errors. The pipefail option is supported by /bin/sh in SUSE Linux Enterprise (SLE) base images, so this change is safe and recommended. This fix addresses only the first occurrence of the issue to comply with the requirement of modifying one issue at a time.

CRITICAL_MESSAGE: Set the SHELL option -o pipefail before RUN with a pipe in it. If you are using /bin/sh in an alpine image or if your shell is symlinked to busybox then consider explicitly setting your SHELL to /bin/ash, or disable this check
FAULT_DESCRIPTION: [DL4006](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint/wiki/DL4006): The Dockerfile contains a RUN command starting at line 2 that uses pipes (|) in the command `$(uname -p)` and potentially in curl operations. Without setting `SHELL ["/bin/sh", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` before this RUN command, if any command in a pipe fails, the overall RUN command may still succeed because the shell only checks the exit status of the last command in the pipe. This can lead to silent failures where errors are not caught during the Docker build process. The pipefail option ensures that the entire pipeline fails if any command within it fails, making the build process more robust and preventing potentially broken images from being created. In SUSE Linux Enterprise (SLE) images, the default shell is typically /bin/sh, so setting pipefail is the recommended approach.
FIX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION: Add a SHELL instruction immediately before the first RUN command (line 2) to enable the pipefail option. Insert `SHELL ["/bin/sh", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` between line 1 (the FROM instruction) and line 2 (the first RUN command). This will ensure that any command failure within a pipe will cause the entire RUN command to fail, making error detection more reliable. The pipefail option is supported by /bin/sh in SUSE-based images. After adding this SHELL instruction, the Docker build will properly fail if any piped command encounters an error, preventing the creation of potentially broken container images.
